# rmux 0.1.6 — preview
This release improves everyday navigation, settings recovery and working with an editor alongside rmux.
- A cleaner command palette with searchable shortcuts, a clear-search button, context-aware group actions and more reliable dismissal and focus recovery. - More consistent workspace selection, tab close buttons, toolbar hints and rename controls. Narrow windows keep more space available for the terminal. - Terminal Find clearly indicates when there are no matches. Tab pickers stay current as tabs open, move and close. - Settings show unsaved appearance changes, let you revert them, and offer **Undo Last Settings Save** while preserving unrelated configuration edits. - Open or reuse a named workspace from an editor with `rmuxctl open-workspace`. Bind configured background commands to shortcuts, including switching back to your editor without opening another terminal. - Open local `file://` terminal links in your configured editor. Recognized remote sessions do not route these links to local files. - Clearer CLI connection errors, steadier diagnostic panels, fewer duplicate group notifications and less sidebar work during rendering. - Help and feedback links are easier to find. macOS update prompts include release notes and a link to the full release.
The website demo shares the palette, navigation and interface improvements. It continues to use sample sessions rather than a real shell; local editor launching and other desktop integrations are not available in the browser.
Packages target macOS Apple Silicon, Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64. The Windows package is unsigned; Linux requires Ubuntu 24.04-compatible libraries. Native Linux/Windows UI and cross-platform performance acceptance remain in progress. Experimental browser windows are not enabled in these release builds.
On macOS, use **rmux → Check for Updates…**. Other platforms update manually.
